title: The law of total probability
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:34Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest card, Multi-stage experiments, adds path probabilities in counter-and-tree problems but never states the law in terms of conditional probabilities given A and given not A, and the conditional probability card does not cover summing over a partition, so no bank point teaches this idea at the right depth.

draft.title: The law of total probability
card: Sometimes an event can happen in more than one way. The law of total probability adds up the chance of each way.
Split on A and not A: Pr(B) = Pr(B | A) × Pr(A) + Pr(B | A') × Pr(A').
Each path is a product: the chance of the first step times the chance of the second step given the first. Then the paths that end in B are added.
draft.remember: Multiply along each path to B, then add the paths.

a.q: Pr(A) = 0.3, Pr(B | A) = 0.6 and Pr(B | A') = 0.1. What is Pr(B)?
a.why: Pr(B) = 0.6 × 0.3 + 0.1 × 0.7 = 0.18 + 0.07 = 0.25. Giving 0.18 counts only the path through A and misses the path through not A.
a.clue: B can happen after A or after not A.

b.q: Priya cycles to school in Geelong on 20% of days, and otherwise takes the bus. She is late on 10% of cycling days and 30% of bus days. What is the probability she is late on a random day?
b.why: Late = 0.1 × 0.2 + 0.3 × 0.8 = 0.02 + 0.24 = 0.26. Giving 0.40 adds 0.1 and 0.3 without weighting each by how often that path is used.
b.clue: Weight each lateness chance by how often she uses that way.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's formula and worked example are correct. Both questions have exactly one right answer: 0.25 for (a) and 0.26 for (b).
